title: I made a Krita plugin that acts like a dynamic palette-snap brush. Would anyone find this useful?
author: vorty92
selftext:
It helps with localized context specific cleanup with a dynamic palette that can be easily modified.

I think it can be useful for pesky cases where sprite-level index color mode in Aseprite messes things up.

I think it could be especially helpful in cleaning up noisy AI output.

Would anyone find this useful?

comments.author: Revelation12Studios
comments.body: Yeah, that looks like it could be helpful.

comments.author: Senior_Chain_4816
comments.body: Bro i would find this so helpful i tried doing the same thing maunally and it took my hours. can you pleaseeee realease it.

replies.author: vorty92
replies.body:
Have you tried using Kritas native **Filter -> Map -> Palettize** and then creating it as a filter mask?

It was brought to my attention that it can do the same thing, and in a non destructive manner since the transformation is tied to the fliter mask. You choose one palette per mask and you can stack multiple of them and then just paint the mask.

Seems like it covers the essentials of the use case with the added burden of Kritas tedious palette management. But that can probably be improved by some type of palette manager plugin instead of this.

That said, would you still prefer a specific tool that does this, like a little pixel cleanup editor? And if so would you pay for it and how much would it be worth it to you?
